title: 20.4 MEMS-Free 4096-Pixel CMOS E-Nose Gas-Sensor Array with Molecular-Selective Metal-Organic-Framework Sensing and In-Pixel Thermodynamic Modulation for Fast Sensor Regeneration
problem: Electronic noses lack sufficient sensor selectivity, suffer from sensor memory effects due to slow gas desorption, and have small sensor arrays without in-pixel processing, limiting real-time gas detection in industrial and safety applications.
motivation: Gas sensing in chemical plants and environmental monitoring requires accurate real-time detection of multiple species (e.g., ammonia) with rapid regeneration to avoid cross-contamination.
method: Monolithic CMOS integration of 4096 molecular-selective MOF (metal-organic-framework) sensors with in-pixel temperature regulation enabling thermodynamic control of gas adsorption/desorption, coupled with local readout and digitization circuits.
key_novelty: In-pixel thermodynamic modulation using temperature regulation to achieve fast sensor regeneration and rapid desorption at the MOF interface.
contributions: Large-scale monolithic 4096-pixel MOF sensor array fabricated in CMOS process
In-pixel temperature regulation enabling rapid desorption and sensitivity enhancement
Integrated capacitance readout and digitization eliminating external signal processing
baselines: prior e-nose implementations with limited selectivity and small arrays
primary_theme: integrated monolithic e-nose with MOF selectivity and thermodynamic regeneration
